articles.title: The American Missile Crisis
articles.summary: Recent global conflicts, including Russia-Ukraine and Iran-Israel, have revealed the fragility of US munitions stockpiles. Extensive direct and indirect involvement in these conflicts has significantly drawn down these reserves. This depletion raises critical concerns about US defense readiness and its long-term capacity to support allies, impacting global strategic stability and military supply chain resilience.

articles.title: The Amazon’s ancient drainage system once ran the other way, carrying water and sediment westward across South America before the rise of the Andes, shifting land levels, and massive sediment buildup helped turn it into the east-flowing river we know today.
articles.summary: The Amazon, Earth's largest river by volume, originates in the Andes mountains and flows eastward across the vast South American continent. It ultimately discharges into the Atlantic Ocean. This immense hydrological system, spanning multiple nations, represents a critical international geographical feature and a powerful force of nature.

articles.title: At least 22 killed in Russian attack; Ukrainian president says new assault possible
articles.summary: Russia launched a massive aerial assault on Ukraine early Tuesday, employing hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles. The attacks tragically killed 22 and wounded 130 people nationwide. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warned of a possible new Russian ground offensive, highlighting the escalating conflict and significant humanitarian cost.
